blocks.text: Setting up Google Sheets for product managers on Mac

Google Sheets is a web app. It does not have a native Mac installer. You should use Google Chrome for the best performance on macOS. To make it feel like a real app, turn it into a Progressive Web App. Open your sheet in Chrome. Click the three-dot menu, select Cast, Save, and Share, then choose Install page as app. This puts a dedicated icon in your Dock.
Essential Google Sheets tips for product management

Product managers often manage large datasets. Use [freeze rows](/how-to/freeze-the-top-row-in-google-sheets) to keep headers visible while scrolling. Use [filters](/how-to/add-a-filter-to-a-range-in-google-sheets) to hide irrelevant data during meetings. If you have duplicate rows from multiple sources, use the built-in tool to [remove them](/how-to/remove-duplicate-rows-in-google-sheets). Always keep your raw data on one tab and your summary dashboard on another.
Using keyboard shortcuts to save time

Stop clicking through menus. Use shortcuts to move faster. Press ⌘ + / to open the full list of shortcuts. Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H for Find and Replace. Use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9 to hide rows and ⌘ + ⌥ + 0 to hide columns. If you are lost, use Option + / to open the tool finder and type what you need.

Collaboration is the core of product management. You might need to [share view only access](/how-to/share-with-view-only-access-in-google-sheets) with stakeholders to prevent accidental edits. If your sheet gets messy, check the [revision history](/how-to/see-revision-history-in-google-sheets) to see who changed what. When you need to move data to a presentation, [export as PDF](/how-to/export-as-pdf-in-google-sheets) or [download as Excel](/how-to/download-as-excel-in-google-sheets).

Google Sheets allows up to 20 million cells. Large sheets get slow. Avoid complex formulas in every cell. Use Pivot Tables for aggregation. If you must use formulas, use ARRAYFORMULA to keep the sheet light. If you hit a wall, break the data into separate files by year or project.

items: Keeping all data in one massive, unformatted sheet.
Hardcoding values instead of using cell references.
Forgetting to lock cells in formulas before dragging them.
Not using named ranges for complex calculations.
Ignoring the warning signs of a slow sheet until it crashes.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No. Google Sheets is a web application. You can create a desktop shortcut using the Install page as app feature in Google Chrome.

faq.question: What is the cell limit in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: As of September 2026, the limit is 20 million cells per spreadsheet.

faq.question: How do I see keyboard shortcuts in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + / on your keyboard to open the shortcut helper window.
